examples.en: The neighbors laid out a feast table so loaded its legs nearly broke.

examples.ko: 할머니 생신날 잔칫상 앞에 온 가족이 모였어요.
examples.en: On Grandma's birthday, the whole family gathered around the feast table.
The rice cakes on the feast table were really delicious.
After the wedding, the feast table was crowded with guests.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁은 잔칫상처럼 푸짐하게 차려 봤어요.
examples.en: Tonight I tried setting out dinner as lavishly as a feast.
I'll call you as soon as the feast table is all set.

explain: '잔치'를 하는 날의 상이라서 평소 밥상보다 음식이 훨씬 많고 화려해요. 평소 식사 자리는 그냥 '밥상'이라고 하고, 잔칫상은 생일이나 결혼 같은 기쁜 날 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.example: 명절이라 어머니가 상다리가 부러지게 음식을 차리셨어요.
phrases.en: Since it was a holiday, Mom set out so much food that the table legs nearly broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 아주 많이 푸짐하게 차렸을 때 쓰는 과장된 표현이에요. 보통 '상다리가 부러지게 차리다'라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration for a table piled with food. It is usually said as '상다리가 부러지게 차리다'.

explain_en: It is the table for a celebration, so it holds far more and fancier food than an everyday meal table. An ordinary meal is just '밥상', while 잔칫상 comes up in talk about happy occasions like birthdays and weddings.

examples.en: I trimmed the fine hair on my face with a razor.

examples.ko: 복숭아 껍질에는 잔털이 많이 나 있어요.
examples.en: Peach skin has a lot of fine fuzz on it.

examples.ko: 제 얼굴의 잔털은 햇빛에 금색으로 보여요.
examples.en: The fine hair on my face looks golden in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 아기는 이마와 볼에 잔털도 나 있어요.
examples.en: The baby has fine hair on the forehead and cheeks too.

examples.ko: 잔털 제거 크림을 써 봤는데 피부가 따가웠어요.
examples.en: I tried a hair removal cream, but my skin stung.
It was so scary that even the fine hairs on my neck stood up.

explain: '솜털'과 비슷하지만, '잔털'은 얼굴, 팔, 다리에 난 가늘고 짧은 털을 말할 때 폭넓게 써요. 굵고 진한 털은 그냥 '털'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '솜털' (down), but 잔털 is used broadly for thin, short hairs on the face, arms and legs. Thick, dark hair is just called '털'.

examples.en: We need to work out whose fault it is.

examples.ko: 일의 잘잘못을 가리기 전에 먼저 사과부터 했어요.
examples.en: Before sorting out who was right or wrong, I apologized first.
I fought with my friend, but we were about equally to blame.

examples.ko: 이제 잘잘못 따지지 말고 같이 해결해요.
examples.en: Let's stop arguing about who's at fault and solve it together.
Regardless of who was at fault, I said sorry first.

examples.ko: 아이들 싸움의 잘잘못이 쉽게 가려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: It wasn't easy to tell who was at fault in the kids' fight.

explain: '잘못'은 틀린 점만 가리키지만 '잘잘못'은 잘한 것과 잘못한 것을 같이 말해요. 보통 '잘잘못을 가리다', '잘잘못을 따지다'처럼 싸움이나 분쟁에서 시비를 가릴 때 써요.
explain_en: '잘못' only points to what was wrong, while 잘잘못 covers both what was done well and what was done wrong. It is mostly used as '잘잘못을 가리다/따지다' when sorting out who is right in a quarrel or dispute.

examples.ko: 잠결에 전화를 받아서 무슨 말을 했는지 몰라요.
examples.en: I answered the phone half asleep, so I don't know what I said.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 일은 잠결이라 잘 기억나지 않아요.
examples.en: I was half asleep last night, so I don't remember it well.
The child recognizes Mom's voice even in their sleep.
My younger sibling got up half asleep and went to the bathroom.
It was just something said half asleep, so don't mind it.
It felt like a doze, and I couldn't tell if it was real or a dream.

explain: 거의 '잠결에' 형태로 써서, 잠이 덜 깬 상태에서 한 말이나 행동을 나타내요. '자다가'는 그냥 자는 도중이라는 뜻이고, '잠결에'는 정신이 흐릿했다는 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '잠결에' for something said or done while not fully awake. '자다가' just means 'while sleeping', but 잠결에 adds the feeling of being foggy and unaware.

examples.en: The diver slowly went down into the sea.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 십 년째 잠수부로 일하고 계세요.
examples.en: My uncle has worked as a diver for ten years.
Divers are examining the sunken ship.
A diver goes into the water carrying an oxygen tank.
When I was little, my dream was to be a diver.

examples.ko: 구조 현장에 잠수부를 열 명 더 보냈어요.
examples.en: They sent ten more divers to the rescue site.

explain: 일이나 구조 작업으로 물속에 들어가는 사람을 말할 때 자주 써요. 취미로 스쿠버 다이빙을 하는 사람은 '다이버'라고도 많이 불러요.
explain_en: It is commonly used for people who go underwater for work or rescue operations. People who scuba dive as a hobby are also often called '다이버'.

en: put someone to sleep; get someone to bed

examples.en: Mom held the baby in her arms and put him to sleep.

examples.ko: 아이를 잠재우는 데 한 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a whole hour to get the child to sleep.
Try putting the child to sleep with a lullaby.

examples.ko: 아기를 겨우 잠재우고 나서 설거지를 했어요.
examples.en: After barely getting the baby to sleep, I did the dishes.
I turned off the room light to get my younger sibling to sleep.

examples.ko: 아이를 잠재운 뒤에 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.en: I'll watch a movie after I put the kids to bed.

explain: 주로 아기나 아이를 재울 때 쓰고, 반대말은 '깨우다'예요. 사람 말고도 소문이나 불안 같은 것을 가라앉힌다는 뜻으로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The director's apology put the controversy to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 재우는 뜻이 아니라, 시끄러운 논란이나 소문을 조용히 가라앉힌다는 뜻이에요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This isn't about putting a person to sleep; it means quieting down a noisy controversy or rumor. It often appears in the news.

explain_en: It is mostly used for getting a baby or child to sleep, and its opposite is '깨우다' (to wake). It can also be used for calming down things like rumors or anxiety.

examples.en: They say dreams are influenced by the subconscious.

examples.ko: 잠재의식 속에 불안이 남아 있었나 봐요.
examples.en: Anxiety must have remained in my subconscious.
Those words stayed deep in my subconscious.
I heard that ads stimulate the subconscious.

examples.ko: 잠재의식은 우리도 모르게 행동에 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: The subconscious affects our actions without us knowing.
If I repeat positive words, will my subconscious change?

explain: '무의식'과 비슷하게 쓰이지만, 일상 대화에서는 '나도 모르게 마음속에 있는 생각'이라는 느낌으로 말할 때 많이 써요. 심리나 자기계발 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is close to '무의식' (the unconscious), but in everyday talk it often means thoughts lying in your mind without you realizing. It comes up a lot in psychology and self-improvement topics.

examples.ko: 건강을 위해 흰쌀 대신 잡곡을 먹어요.
examples.en: For my health, I eat mixed grains instead of white rice.
I looked around the mixed grains section at the mart.
Mixed grains are chewier than rice.

examples.ko: 보리와 콩 같은 잡곡이 밥에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Grains like barley and beans go well in rice.
This shop sells only domestically grown grains.
They say mixed grains have a lot of dietary fiber.

explain: 쌀을 뺀 보리, 콩, 수수, 조 같은 곡식을 한데 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 건강 이야기에서 '흰쌀'과 대비해서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It groups together grains other than rice, such as barley, beans, sorghum and millet. It often appears in health talk as a contrast to '흰쌀' (white rice).

examples.en: These days I eat multigrain rice every morning.
Multigrain rice is a bit coarser than white rice.
I ate multigrain rice with seasoned vegetable side dishes.
I switched because they say multigrain rice is good for health.
Please give me multigrain rice, not white rice.
Does this restaurant offer multigrain rice too?

explain: 쌀에 보리, 콩, 수수 같은 여러 곡식을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 보리만 섞으면 '보리밥', 현미로 지으면 '현미밥'이라고 따로 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is rice cooked with a mix of grains such as barley, beans and sorghum. If only barley is mixed in it is called '보리밥', and rice made with brown rice is '현미밥'.

examples.en: Grandfather is enjoying his breakfast.
The elder finished eating and got up.
I hope you'll eat the stew before it gets cold.

examples.ko: 아버지는 아침에 빵을 잘 잡수시지 않아요.
examples.en: My father doesn't often eat bread in the morning.
The teacher has already had lunch.
I cooked porridge for Grandmother to eat.

explain: '드시다'와 함께 어른께 쓰는 높임말인데, 보통 '잡수세요', '잡수셨어요'처럼 '-시-'를 붙여서 말해요. 나 자신이나 아랫사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 밥의 높임말 '진지'와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Like '드시다', it is an honorific for elders, and it is usually said with '-시-' added, as in '잡수세요' or '잡수셨어요'. Never use it for yourself or someone younger. It often appears with '진지', the honorific word for a meal.

examples.en: The rabbit almost got eaten by the fox.
I told a story about someone eaten by a tiger.
Small fish get eaten by big fish.

examples.ko: 비둘기는 도망가려 했지만 결국 매에게 잡아먹히고 말았어요.
examples.en: The pigeon tried to escape but was eventually caught and eaten by a hawk.
The rabbit hid in a burrow so it wouldn't be eaten.
I saw a scene of a frog being eaten by a snake.

explain: 잡아먹는 쪽에는 '에게'나 '한테'를 붙여요. 짝이 되는 능동형은 '잡아먹다'예요. 그냥 '먹히다'보다 붙잡혀서 죽임을 당한다는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
explain_en: The one doing the eating takes '에게' or '한테'. Its active counterpart is '잡아먹다'. Compared with plain '먹히다', it makes clearer that the victim is caught and killed.

examples.en: A pickpocket suddenly snatched my bag.
When I jerked the fishing rod, a big fish came up.

examples.ko: 그는 내 손목을 잡아채서 밖으로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: He grabbed my wrist and pulled me outside.
A motorcycle came closer to snatch the bag.
Please don't take things as if you're snatching them.
The person who snatched the wallet ran away.

explain: 갑자기 힘을 주어 확 잡아당겨 가지는 동작이에요. 가방 날치기나 낚시에서 자주 나오고, '낚아채다'와 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It describes grabbing something and yanking it suddenly with force. It often appears in bag-snatching and fishing contexts, and is used much like '낚아채다'.

examples.en: I put on concealer to cover the blemishes on my face.
My skin is fair, so blemishes show up easily.

examples.ko: 잡티까지 한 번에 없애 주는 크림이래요.
examples.en: They say it's a cream that even clears blemishes at once.

examples.ko: 햇빛을 많이 받으면 잡티는 더 짙어져요.
examples.en: If you get a lot of sun, blemishes get darker.

examples.ko: 잡티 때문에 화장이 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: Because of the blemishes, makeup doesn't go on well.

examples.ko: 잡티에 효과가 있는 팩을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a mask that works on blemishes.

explain: 기미, 주근깨, 점처럼 피부에 생긴 작은 얼룩이나 잡스러운 자국을 뭉뚱그려 부르는 말이에요. 화장품이나 피부 관리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It loosely covers small marks on the skin such as melasma, freckles and spots. It comes up often in talk about cosmetics and skin care.

examples.ko: 산에 잣나무 숲이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: A pine forest of Korean nut pines stretches along the mountain.
In autumn, pine nuts grow on the Korean nut pine.
Grandfather planted a Korean nut pine in the yard.
The Korean nut pine stays green even in winter.
The nut pines along the road were covered in snow.
That child grew up straight like a nut pine.

explain: 열매인 '잣'이 열리는 나무예요. 소나무와 비슷해 보이지만 소나무는 잎이 두 개씩, 잣나무는 다섯 개씩 모여 나서 구분할 수 있어요. 발음은 [잔나무]예요.
explain_en: It is the tree that bears pine nuts ('잣'). It looks like a '소나무' (red pine), but needles grow in pairs on a 소나무 and in bundles of five on a 잣나무, so you can tell them apart. It is pronounced [잔나무].

examples.en: My parents felt relieved after marrying off their son.
When are you going to marry off your son?
Since we married off our eldest son, the house is quiet.
If we marry off even the youngest, I'll have no more wishes.
I saved money hard to marry off my son.

examples.ko: 장가보낼 나이가 됐는데 연애도 안 해요.
examples.en: He's old enough to be married off, but he isn't even dating.

explain: 아들을 결혼시킨다는 말에만 써요. 딸을 결혼시킬 때는 '시집보내다'라고 해요. 주로 부모나 어른이 주어가 되고, 짝이 되는 말은 '장가가다'예요.
explain_en: This is used only for marrying off a son. For a daughter you say '시집보내다'. The subject is usually a parent or elder, and its counterpart is '장가가다' (for a man to marry).

examples.ko: 이번 협상은 장기전이 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This negotiation looks like it will be a long haul.

examples.ko: 회사는 장기전에 대비해서 자금을 모아 뒀어요.
examples.en: The company saved funds to prepare for a long fight.

examples.ko: 시험 준비는 장기전이니까 체력 관리도 중요해요.
examples.en: Exam prep is a long game, so managing stamina matters too.
We should treat it as a long game, not a short one.
The final was decided after a long drawn-out battle.
I started it prepared for a long struggle from the beginning.

explain: 반대말은 '단기전'이에요. 전쟁이나 경기뿐 아니라 시험, 협상, 다이어트처럼 오래 걸릴 일을 비유할 때도 일상에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '단기전' (a short battle). Beyond wars and games, people often use it figuratively for things that take a long time, like exams, negotiations or diets.

examples.en: I'm worried about the economic slump dragging on.
As the war dragged on, prices went up.

examples.ko: 공사 장기화로 주민들이 불편을 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: Residents are suffering inconvenience because the construction is dragging on.
The situation is likely to drag on.

examples.ko: 파업 장기화에 따라 피해가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Damage is growing as the strike drags on.

examples.ko: 문제가 장기화되지 않도록 빨리 해결해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to solve the problem quickly so it doesn't drag on.

explain: 뉴스에서 '~이/가 장기화되다' 형태로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '오래 끌다', '길어지다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In the news it often appears as '~이/가 장기화되다'. In everyday conversation people usually say '오래 끌다' or '길어지다' instead.

examples.en: It's market day, so there's a lot to see at the market.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 오 일에 한 번 장날이 서요.
examples.en: In our town, market day comes once every five days.
Grandma goes out to sell vegetables every market day.

examples.ko: 장날에 가면 싱싱한 나물을 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go on market day, you can buy fresh greens cheaply.
Do you know when the next market day is?
Today is market day, so the roads are really jammed.

explain: 오일장처럼 정해진 날에 열리는 시장이 서는 날이에요. 요즘 도시에서는 매일 가게가 열려서 시골이나 전통 시장 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 그 식당에 갔는데 가는 날이 장날이라고 문을 닫았더라고요.
phrases.en: I went to that restaurant for the first time in a while, and just my luck, it was closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 있어서 갔더니 공교롭게도 일이 꼬였을 때 쓰는 속담이에요. 보통 운이 나쁘거나 타이밍이 안 맞았을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb for when you go somewhere and things unluckily turn out wrong. It is mostly said about bad luck or bad timing.

explain_en: It is the day a periodic market, like a five-day market, is held. Because city shops open every day, it appears mostly in talk about the countryside and traditional markets.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 장대높이뛰기 세계 기록을 세웠어요.
examples.en: That athlete set a world record in the pole vault.
I saw the pole vault for the first time at a sports day.
The pole vault looks really hard technically.

examples.ko: 올림픽 장대높이뛰기 결승을 보느라 밤을 샜어요.
examples.en: I stayed up all night watching the Olympic pole vault final.
My younger sibling won a gold medal in the pole vault.

examples.ko: 장대높이뛰기도 배울 수 있는 학원이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a place where I can learn the pole vault too?

explain: 긴 장대를 이용해 바를 넘는 육상 종목이에요. 장대 없이 뛰어서 넘는 '높이뛰기'와는 다른 종목이에요. 발음은 [장대노피뛰기]예요.
explain_en: It is a track-and-field event in which you clear a bar with the help of a long pole. It differs from '높이뛰기' (high jump), which is jumping without a pole. It is pronounced [장대노피뛰기].

en: large earthenware jar for sauces and pastes

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 장독대에는 항아리가 줄지어 있어요.
examples.en: At Grandma's house, jars stand in a row on the jar terrace.
These days it is hard to find a jar terrace in an apartment.
I opened the jar lid and scooped out some soybean paste.

examples.ko: 시골집 마당에는 장독이 열 개쯤 있어요.
examples.en: There are about ten sauce jars in the country house yard.
Every sauce jar has a name tag on it.

examples.ko: 엄마가 빈 장독을 깨끗이 닦아 말리셨어요.
examples.en: Mom wiped the empty sauce jar clean and dried it.

explain: '장독'은 항아리 자체이고, 그 항아리들을 모아 놓는 마당 한쪽 자리는 '장독대'라고 해요. 요즘 도시에서는 보기 어려워서 시골이나 옛날 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '장독' is the jar itself, and the spot in the yard where such jars are gathered is called '장독대'. They are hard to find in cities today, so they come up mostly in stories about the countryside or the past.

examples.en: After walking a long time, my calves hurt.
I got a cramp in my calf while sleeping.
After I rubbed my calf, it loosened up a bit.
My calf muscles are well developed.
I got a calf massage after the marathon.
Calves get firm quickly when you exercise.

explain: '종아리'와 비슷하지만 '장딴지'는 종아리 뒤쪽 불룩한 근육 부분을 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '종아리'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is close to '종아리' (lower leg), but 장딴지 points to the bulging muscle on the back of the lower leg. In daily conversation people also often just say '종아리'.

examples.en: This restaurant's soy-based sauces taste deep and nutty.
The taste of jang differs a little from house to house.
To taste the jang, try the soybean paste soup first.
It's a house famous for its good jang.
The longer it ages, the deeper the flavor of the jang gets.
Customers are won over by the jang and come often.

explain: '장'은 간장, 된장, 고추장을 함께 부르는 말이라, 장맛은 이런 발효 양념의 맛을 말해요. 장마철을 뜻하는 '장마'와 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요. 발음은 [장맏]이에요.
explain_en: '장' is a collective word for soy sauce, soybean paste and red pepper paste, so 장맛 is the taste of these fermented seasonings. Don't confuse it with '장마' (the rainy season). It is pronounced [장맏].

examples.en: She wrapped a rose-colored scarf around her head.
The evening sky turned rosy.
The baby's cheeks are flushed and rosy.
I worked hard, dreaming of a rosy future.
But reality wasn't rosy.
A pretty rose-pink petal fell.

explain: '분홍빛'보다 장미꽃처럼 붉은 기가 도는 연한 색을 말해요. 색깔 외에 '밝고 희망적인'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 발음은 [장미삗]이에요.

phrases.example: 졸업만 하면 장밋빛 미래가 펼쳐질 줄 알았어요.
phrases.en: I thought a rosy future would open up once I graduated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 색이 아니라 앞날이 매우 밝고 희망차다는 뜻이에요. 현실은 그렇지 않다는 말과 같이 쓰일 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not refer to an actual color but to a bright, hopeful future. It is often used together with the idea that reality isn't that way.

explain_en: Compared with '분홍빛' (pink), it points to a light color with a red tint, like a rose. Beyond color it is often used figuratively for 'bright and hopeful'. It is pronounced [장미삗].

examples.en: I'm the eldest grandson, so my grandfather cherishes me.
He was born as the eldest grandson of the family.
On the holiday, the eldest grandson bowed first.
Grandma dotes on the eldest grandson the most.
My older brother, the eldest grandson, took over the family.
Grandfather handed down the old family register to the eldest grandson.

explain: 집안의 대를 잇는 맏손자를 가리켜요. 아들의 아들 중 맏이를 말하고, '장남'(맏아들)과 구분해서 써요. 전통을 중시하는 집안 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the eldest grandson who carries on the family line. It is used for the eldest of the sons' sons and is kept distinct from '장남' (eldest son). It comes up often when talking about families that value tradition.

examples.en: I took the Christmas decorations out of the box.
I made this ornament myself.
The ornaments hanging on the tree are sparkling.
I hung a small picture as a wall decoration.
Dust has piled up on the decorations.

examples.ko: 장식물 하나 때문에 방 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The room's mood changed because of a single ornament.

explain: 꾸미기 위해 놓거나 다는 물건을 두루 가리켜요. '장식품'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 둘 다 집이나 행사 분위기를 꾸밀 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to things placed or hung for decoration. '장식품' is used in a similar way, and both come up often when decorating a home or an event.

examples.en: I brought a new display cabinet into the living room.

examples.ko: 장식장 안에 여행에서 사 온 기념품이 있어요.
examples.en: There are souvenirs from my trips inside the display cabinet.
Grandma's display cabinet is full of ceramics.
This display cabinet has glass doors.

examples.ko: 장식장이 너무 커서 거실이 좁아 보여요.
examples.en: The display cabinet is so big that the living room looks small.
I'm using it as a display cabinet instead of a bookcase.

explain: 물건을 넣어 두는 가구가 아니라 보여 주려고 두는 물건을 진열하는 장이에요. 책을 꽂는 '책장', 옷이나 물건을 넣는 '서랍장'과 구분해서 불러요.
explain_en: It is a cabinet for showing off items rather than just storing them. It is distinguished from a '책장' (bookcase) and a '서랍장' (chest of drawers).

en: pickled vegetables (preserved in soy sauce or paste)

examples.en: I ate pickled chili peppers as a side dish with rice.
Jangajji is salty, so it goes well with rice.
This restaurant's jangajji is really tasty.

examples.ko: 깻잎 장아찌 한 장이면 밥 한 그릇 뚝딱이에요.
examples.en: One pickled perilla leaf is enough to finish a bowl of rice.
I bought radishes to use for pickling.

examples.ko: 오래 두고 먹으려고 장아찌처럼 절여 두었어요.
examples.en: I pickled it like jangajji so I could keep it a long time.

explain: 무, 마늘, 깻잎, 고추 같은 채소를 간장이나 된장, 고추장에 절여 만든 반찬이에요. 김치와 달리 짭짤해서 조금씩 집어 먹는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a side dish of vegetables like radish, garlic, perilla leaves or chili peppers preserved in soy sauce or fermented pastes. Unlike kimchi it is salty, so people usually eat just a little at a time.

examples.en: I got a call from the hospital telling me to come in for a retest.
The result was unclear, so they say a retest is needed.
The retest results come out next week.
I went back to the hospital for a retest.
The retest came back normal, so I was relieved.
Does a retest cost money again?

explain: '재검사를 받다', '재검사를 하다'처럼 써요. 건강검진뿐 아니라 제품 품질 검사나 시험에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 병원 이야기에서 가장 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It is used as '재검사를 받다' or '재검사를 하다'. It also applies to product quality checks and exams, but in daily life you meet it most often in talk about hospitals.

examples.en: I reorganized the order of the story and rewrote it.
We decided to rearrange the office seating.

examples.ko: 사건 현장을 재구성해 보니 단서가 보였어요.
examples.en: When we reconstructed the scene, clues appeared.

examples.ko: 수업 내용을 재구성한 자료를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: They handed out materials with the lesson content restructured.
The presentation order needs to be reorganized.
The reorganizing took a lot of time.

explain: 이미 있는 내용이나 구조를 다시 짜 맞춘다는 느낌이에요. 글, 수업 자료, 사건 설명 등에 두루 쓰고, 보통 '재구성하다' 형태로 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of putting existing content or structure together again. It is used broadly for writing, lesson materials and accounts of events, and is usually said as '재구성하다'.

examples.en: While traveling, I experienced a rediscovery of myself.

examples.ko: 이 책의 주제는 한국 음식의 재발견이에요.
examples.en: The theme of this book is the rediscovery of Korean food.

examples.ko: 옛 노래의 재발견 덕분에 다시 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the rediscovery of the old song, it became popular again.
Travel was a kind of rediscovery for me.
The rediscovery of traditional markets is a hot topic.
Rediscovery needs a fresh point of view.

explain: 처음 찾아내는 '발견'과 달리 이미 알고 있던 것의 가치를 새롭게 깨닫는 것을 말해요. 책 제목이나 기사 제목에 '~의 재발견'이라는 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '발견' (finding something for the first time), it means realizing anew the value of something you already knew. It shows up often in book and article titles in the form '~의 재발견'.

examples.en: While reading, I rediscovered the joy of reading.
On the trip, I came to rediscover myself.
I think I've rediscovered how precious family is.

examples.ko: 옛 친구를 만나 서로를 재발견하려고 노력했어요.
examples.en: I met an old friend and we tried to get to know each other anew.

examples.ko: 이번 전시는 한국 그림을 재발견할 좋은 기회예요.
examples.en: This exhibition is a great chance to rediscover Korean painting.

examples.ko: 오래된 동네를 걷다가 숨은 매력을 재발견해요.
examples.en: Walking through an old neighborhood, I rediscover its hidden charm.

explain: 모르던 것을 처음 찾는 '발견하다'와 달리, 알고 있던 것의 좋은 점을 새삼 깨닫는다는 뜻이에요. 사람, 장소, 취미 등에 '~을/를 재발견하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '발견하다' (to find something unknown), it means to newly realize the good in something you already knew. It is used with people, places and hobbies as '~을/를 재발견하다'.

examples.en: My mother made curtains with a sewing machine.
I could hear the sewing machine until late at night.

examples.ko: 재봉틀을 배워서 직접 옷을 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn the sewing machine so I can fix clothes myself.
There is an old sewing machine in Grandma's room.

examples.ko: 재봉틀에 실을 끼워 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you thread the sewing machine for me?

examples.ko: 재봉틀은 바느질을 아주 빠르게 해 줘요.
examples.en: A sewing machine does stitching very fast.

explain: 손으로 하는 바느질과 달리 기계로 박는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '미싱'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: Unlike hand sewing, it is a machine that does the stitching. In daily life many people also call it '미싱'.

examples.en: The constitution protects citizens' property rights.
The landowner claims to hold the property rights.

examples.ko: 아파트 재건축은 주민의 재산권과 관련이 있어요.
examples.en: Apartment reconstruction is related to residents' property rights.
People gathered to protest, calling it an infringement of property rights.
Individual property rights are guaranteed by law.
I consulted a lawyer about the property rights to the land.

explain: 주로 '재산권을 보호하다', '재산권을 침해하다'처럼 법이나 뉴스 이야기에서 나와요. 특허나 저작권 같은 것은 '지식재산권'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in talk about law and the news, as in '재산권을 보호하다' or '재산권을 침해하다'. Things like patents and copyrights are separately called '지식재산권' (intellectual property rights).

examples.ko: 집을 가진 사람은 매년 재산세를 내야 해요.
examples.en: People who own a house must pay property tax every year.
The property tax bill came as soon as I bought the house.
The property tax notice came in the mail.
Do you know how property tax is calculated?
I inquired at the district office about the property tax.
I almost missed the property tax payment deadline.

explain: 집이나 땅 같은 재산을 가진 사람이 내는 세금이에요. 보통 '재산세를 내다', '재산세가 나오다'처럼 말하고, 소득에 매기는 '소득세'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the tax paid by people who own property such as a house or land. People say '재산세를 내다' or '재산세가 나오다', and it differs from '소득세' (income tax), which is charged on earnings.
